reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No direct target engagement data reported for cabozantinib. Only baseline c-Met expression and copy number were measured, but no pharmacodynamic changes showing target modulation were reported. For paclitaxel, target engagement is assumed based on its well-established mechanism. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No biomarker data showing downstream pathway changes for either arm. Cannot assess whether targets drove their intended mechanisms. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The cabozantinib arm failed on both primary endpoint (EFS 3.48 vs 4.96 months for paclitaxel) and secondary endpoint (ORR 7.02% vs 24.07%). Paclitaxel arm succeeded on both endpoints. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: This was an adequately powered head-to-head comparison. The failure appears to be mechanistic - cabozantinib's anti-angiogenic approach was inferior to paclitaxel's cytotoxic approach in this recurrent ovarian cancer population.

failure_modes.evidence: Cabozantinib likely engaged its targets (c-MET/VEGFR2) based on known pharmacology, but the anti-angiogenic biology did not translate to clinical benefit in this recurrent ovarian cancer setting, being inferior to standard cytotoxic therapy
